doc.title: John Fedchock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 28, 2015

chapter: Early training and path to Woody Herman
title: Teacher, Ohio State degrees and the plan to get to Eastman and Woody
summary: He studied with a Cleveland freelance trombonist, did jazz and music ed degrees at Ohio State, and aimed for Eastman after seeing Woody Herman's band at his school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Did it ever occur to you or your parents or your teachers that there was another route besides going to music school, or was that sort of understood if you wanted to pursue this.

Well my first trombone teacher I started with in ninth grade, and aside from about a year and a half he took me all the way through the end of my high school days, was a kind of a freelance guy in Cleveland, Ohio, who played with the big bands. He wasn’t a classical player by any means, but he was one of the more I guess you could say working musicians in the Cleveland area. And even on our lessons we never really practiced diehard classical repertoire. We did technical things, but then we would always end up playing like pop duets and things like that. So I wasn’t really exposed to that kind of element. But when I really got interested in jazz and in music, that’s when I decided I wanted to continue, jazz is what got me excited about it, but at the same time I think it was kind of implied in my family that I was going to college. So I said I’d like to major in music. And really, to be honest, I didn’t think I was strong enough to be a performer at the time so I majored in music education. And then about halfway through my studies at Ohio State University in my undergrad years they started a jazz degree. And so I started taking all the jazz classes too. So I did two degrees, jazz and music ed. And then with the hopes of getting good enough to get into a high powered grad school, Eastman in particular, because when I was in high school Woody Herman’s band came to my school and did a concert and a clinic and I was super stoked because it was like obviously a great band. And they were playing great classic literature but they were also playing very modern things, and the band was full of guys in their twenties. And I thought wow, this is something that’s not just nostalgia and from old records. And I noticed Woody was getting a lot of trombone players from Eastman. So I thought well there’s got to be something there to get me to the next step. So that was kind of my short term goal, just to get good enough to get into Eastman and then from Eastman kind of maybe find a way to get on Woody’s band.
That was good planning on your part.
It was pretty lucky calculations yeah.
